newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine gives Russia 20-year lease of Sevastopol.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine gives Russia 20-year lease of Sevastopol.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said Ukraine agreed on Wednesday to allow Russia to keep its share of the ex-Soviet Black Sea Fleet at Ukraine's naval base of Sevastopol for the next 20 years.

Chernomyrdin made the announcement at a joint news conference with Ukrainian Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko after the two had signed terms of a lease for part of the base. He gave no details of how much Moscow will pay for the lease.

Lazarenko said the lease was part of a package of three deals signed by the prime ministers in Kiev. He said documents also tackled the technical and financial aspects of stationing the Russian and Ukrainian parts of the fleet on the Crimean peninsula.
"The issue of prolonging the lease was not discussed today. Let's take time and see," Lazarenko said. "At least for the first 20 years," Chernomyrdin added.

Chernomyrdin said earlier on Wednesday that he and Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma had solved all outstanding problems in bilateral relations opening the way for a visit to Kiev by Russian President Boris Yeltsin later this week.
Yeltsin and Kuchma are expected to crown their two-day summit by signing a political treaty shaping relations between two former Soviet republics.
